title: Sequenced Launch Playbook: Minimal Viable QoS Lanes and Escalation Matrix for Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank
creator: Ava Chen
description: High-level PRD and sequenced launch/playbook for introducing Minimal Viable QoS lanes (Fast / Balanced / CostOptimized) across Chat, Completions, Embeddings and Rerank endpoints. This doc focuses on acceptance gates tied to telemetry/evals and operational rollback/escalation runbooks so the hosted API can expand capacity while protecting quality and cost objectives.
goals: Ship three QoS lanes for hosted inference: Fast (low latency), Balanced (latency+cost), CostOptimized (throughput/cost savings)
Provide deterministic acceptance criteria per endpoint type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) to gate rollout
Define automated rollback and graded degradation policies driven by signals (latency P95, quality regression, error rate, token cost change)
Ensure runbooks for tenant isolation, canary traffic shaping, and emergency migrations are validated
Integrate eval-driven telemetry and drift detection for embeddings and rerank quality
scope_in: QoS lane selection API surface and route-level config for hosted endpoints
Per-route telemetry dashboards and acceptance gates (quality and perf)
Canary plan with progressive traffic ramps + tenant-aware slices
Launch checklist items for runtime changes: batching defaults, KV cache TTLs, quantization profiles
Evaluation harness for embedding similarity and rerank NDCG regression checks
scope_out: Dedicated capacity (reserved customer clusters) behavior changes
New model family onboarding (out of scope unless explicitly listed in dependencies)
User-facing SDK ergonomics (deferred to SDK team tickets)
acceptance_criteria: Functional: API responds to lane selection parameter and returns lane metadata in /v1/usage header
Perf: For Fast lane, median latency reduction >= 25% vs Balanced for 95th percentile token length profile in synthetic bench
Perf: For CostOptimized lane, token cost per 1k tokens reduced by >= 18% in steady-state microbench
Quality: Chat endpoint behavioural similarity score (BLEU/semantic sim ensemble) must not regress more than 1.5% vs Balanced lane on the baseline eval set
Quality: Embeddings must maintain >= 99.5% of baseline recall@10 on benchmark dataset; drift alert available if below 99%
Quality: Rerank NDCG@5 cannot drop more than 0.8% for production-like evals; blocking if >1.2%
Reliability: Error rate (5xx/4xx rate) increase < 0.3 percentage points relative to baseline during canary
Observability: Telemetry instrumented and visible in Console with token-level cost breakdown, lane-level P50/P95/P99, and quality drift graphs
Rollback: Automated rollback trigger defined and tested in canary (see rollout_plan), and rollback completes within 2 minutes for route-level config changes
launch_checklist: Finalize API contract: lane query param + response headers -- API review complete (owner: Diego)
Docs: Lightweight API docs + Quickstart snippet (owner: DevEx)
PRs: Runtime batching/quantization defaults merged and smoke-tested (links below)
Evals: Baseline eval suites for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank executed and results archived
Dashboards: Per-lane consoles and alerting enabled in Console (owner: Observability)
Canary: Canary slice list defined (tenant IDs + synthetic traffic) and schedule booked
Playbook: Escalation matrix and postmortem checklist added to runbook
Security: KMS key rotation and audit log sampling validated (security sign-off obtained)
Billing: Billing meter for lane usage validated against accounting rules
Support: Support KB created with triage steps and SLO expectations
Chaos: One controlled failure test (node preemption) executed during canary and results logged
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal preview: 0% public traffic, internal tenants + smoke (2 days)
Phase 1 - Tenant canary: select 5 low-risk tenants at 2% traffic cumulatively (48 hours), monitor signals
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 5 days if gates pass
Phase 3 - Wide availability: open to self-serve + incentives for early adopters
Partitioning: Canary uses tenant-aware weighted routing to avoid blast radius; per-tenant kill switch must be tested
Rollback triggers: latency P95 increase > 40% or quality regression above thresholds (see acceptance_criteria) or error rate jump > 0.3 points
Degraded-mode policy: If capacity contention detected, automatically fallback to Balanced lane for affected tenants
telemetry: Metrics: lane.p50_ms, lane.p95_ms, lane.p99_ms, lane.token_cost_per_1k, lane.error_rate, lane.token_throughput
Drift: daily similarity drift calculated with rolling window; alert if 3-sigma drift persists for 24h
Tracing: end-to-end request trace with model variant and kernel selection tags
dependencies: PM-362000 (billing: lane usage metering and pricing calibration)
SEC-1298 (security: audit log schema and KMS integration)

open_questions: Do we expose lane selection as a first-class field in SDKs or keep it as a header only? (tradeoff: discoverability vs breaking API ergonomics)
Should we allow tenant-level override for default lane assignment? requires billing decision for cost attribution.
Is there appetite to auto-profile workloads and recommend lane for customers as a future enhancement?
